intro.text: A combined Alethi attack deep into the Shattered Plains, which Dalinar Kholin proposed to bring the highprinces together, finish the War of Reckoning and fulfil the Vengeance Pact.
A battle at Narak, deep in the Shattered Plains, between four Alethi armies and the Parshendi, during which the Parshendi summoned the Everstorm.

items.text: Hoping to unite the highprinces and end the war, Dalinar proposed a joint push into the heart of the Plains, and the forces of Aladar, Kholin, Roion and Sebarial marched out during the Weeping, a four-week stretch with no highstorm.

Meanwhile most of the Parshendi had taken stormform, a powerful new form; a few who saw what it did refused and fled Narak. Led by Eshonai, the rest prepared to summon a storm against the arriving Alethi.

On the march Shallan Davar showed Dalinar her Lightweaving. At Narak the Alethi met Rlain, who said something had turned his people into monsters, and Dalinar sent Shallan to find the Oathgate to Urithiru so the army could escape if needed.
The Parshendi held three plateaus, so the Alethi split up: Roion, Aladar and Adolin Kholin each attacked one while Dalinar commanded from a fourth.
As Adolin's force charged, red lightning killed his horse Sureblood, threw him from the saddle and cut down many of his soldiers.
On Roion's plateau the Parshendi got the upper hand: the Kholin Shardbearer Teleb fell and Roion's army was routed.
Advised by Rlain, Dalinar ordered his troops to kill the Parshendi singing at the rear before they could finish their song. Adolin's group broke through a wall and ambushed them from behind.
Adolin fought Eshonai and knocked her into a chasm; the bridgemen Skar and Drehy and other soldiers caught him before he went over the edge too.

Szeth, whom Taravangian had secretly sent to assassinate Dalinar, met Adolin and fought him. Aladar won his plateau, but too late: the singers summoned the Everstorm, and an unexpected highstorm approached from the other side, both heading to meet over Narak.

Shallan guessed that a perfectly round plateau, out of keeping with the rest of the Plains, held the Oathgate. Taking Renarin Kholin along with soldiers and scholars, she found it, and learned that it worked like a fabrial and needed a living Shardblade.
Szeth beat Adolin and attacked Dalinar, killing Roion when he came to help, then Lashed Dalinar into the sky to fall to his death. Kaladin arrived, saved Dalinar and took on Szeth.
Dalinar led the retreat to the Oathgate, and the armies escaped before the storms met. Above them Kaladin and Szeth fought with Surgebinding until Kaladin won and took Szeth's Honorblade.
Kaladin reached the Oathgate plateau with the Honorblade, where the rest of Bridge Four told him how to work the gate, and he rejoined the survivors in Urithiru.
Szeth's body was found and brought back to life by Nale, who took him as an apprentice and handed him Nightblood.

Hearing that Urithiru had been found and fearing the Everstorm, the Bethab, Hatham, Ruthar and Sadeas warcamps moved there on Dalinar's orders. Hatham had recharged his spheres in the surprise highstorm, which made him rich while others went short of Stormlight during the Weeping.
The Alethi armies had been badly mauled. Thanadal and Vamah, whose forces were now the strongest, stayed in the warcamps and refused to back Dalinar's plans for Urithiru.
The Sons of Honor counted the battle a win, since they had worked to bring back the Voidbringers and a new Desolation.
It was a win for the Ghostbloods too, whose immediate goal had been finding Urithiru. Seeing Shallan use her powers in the battle, Mraize urged her to join them properly.
